references.text: Moses appointed the cities of refuge east of the Jordan, including Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan, as a parallel to the cities west of the Jordan mentioned in Joshua 20:7.
The law concerning the cities of refuge that Moses gave, which Joshua 20:7 fulfills by designating the specific cities.
God's command to Moses to appoint six cities of refuge, which Joshua 20:7 partially carries out.
Kedesh in Galilee is mentioned again as a Levitical city and a city of refuge, confirming its status from Joshua 20:7.
Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim is mentioned as a Levitical city and a city of refuge, in accordance with Joshua 20:7.
Kiriath-Arba (Hebron) in the hill country of Judah was given to Caleb, but the city itself became a city of refuge as in Joshua 20:7.
Kiriath-Arba is identified as Hebron, the city of Arbah, the ancestor of the Anakim, the same place as in Joshua 20:7.
Hebron is mentioned as the place where Sarah died, highlighting the historical significance of the city that later became a city of refuge.
Kedesh in Naphtali is mentioned as the home of Barak, the same city that was designated as a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7.
A parallel list of the cities of refuge confirming Kedesh, Shechem, and Hebron from Joshua 20:7.
